brief.headline: Move from 100% advance to 30-day credit — our strongest, simplest win worth ₹8.73 L in working capital — then close the ₹12.95 L price gap to Sayaji's ₹66.48/KG.

priceAsk.summary: Match Sayaji's ₹66.48/KG for Dextrose, closing the current 6.5% gap
priceAsk.target: ₹66.48/KG (our best price from Sayaji Industries Limited), saving ₹12.95 L annually
priceAsk.basis: We already pay ₹66.48/KG to Sayaji Industries Limited for the same material; paying them ₹70.80/KG creates a 6.5% gap and costs us ₹12.95 L extra per year. India export unit value sits at 42.95 ₹/kg, showing the market runs well below both prices — ₹66.48/KG is our internal benchmark, not an aggressive outlier.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Shift from 100% advance to standard 30-day credit
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: ₹8.73 L working capital freed if we move to 30-day terms

brief.financialLeverage: Sukhjit runs ₹1458.95 Cr revenue but only a 2.3% net margin and 5.9% return on capital — thin profitability that limits room for deep price cuts. Their D (33/100) health score signals fragility; squeezing too hard risks destabilising a supplier. Debt-to-equity of 0.61x is moderate, not alarming. We represent just 0.07% of their revenue (₹1.06 Cr), so we have negligible standalone leverage. Lead with the payment-terms ask — it costs them little and delivers real cash relief to us — then use the Sayaji benchmark and credible alternates to justify the price move without threatening their viability.

evidence.point: We pay ₹70.80/KG; Sayaji delivers the same material at ₹66.48/KG
The 6.5% gap costs us ₹12.95 L every year in avoidable excess
We pay 100% in advance; moving to 30-day terms frees ₹8.73 L working capital

evidence.point: India's dextrose export unit value is 42.95 ₹/kg — the market runs far below our current price
Sukhjit's net margin is 2.3% and health score D (33/100) — thin profitability, fragile footing
Our ₹1.06 Cr spend is 0.07% of their ₹1458.95 Cr revenue — we're a rounding error

alternates.name: Gulshan Polyols Ltd
alternates.why: Listed starch & polyol maker, ₹2359.06 Cr revenue, B (62/100) health — established dextrose supplier, financially stronger, drop-in alternate to our current sources.

alternates.name: Sanstar Ltd
alternates.why: Recently-listed maize-derivatives specialist (starch, dextrose), ₹821.13 Cr revenue, C (53/100) health — growing capacity, credible second source.

alternates.name: Tirupati Starch & Chemicals Ltd
alternates.why: Listed Indore wet-miller, ₹365.39 Cr revenue, makes Dextrose ANHYDROUS (IV-fluid grade) matching our spec — exact form match pending CoA confirmation.

risks: We're 0.07% of their revenue — negligible leverage alone; bundle volume commitment or multi-year term to gain weight.
2.3% net margin and D (33/100) health: pushing a hard price cut risks tipping a fragile supplier and losing supply continuity.
100% advance terms mean they're cash-cautious or risk-averse; expect resistance to credit — frame 30-day as industry-standard, not a concession.
No borrowing-cost data means we can't quantify an early-payment discount; stick to benchmark pricing and standard terms rather than creative finance levers.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We'd like to move to standard 30-day credit — that frees ₹8.73 L for us and aligns you with how we work with every other supplier — and then talk about closing the gap to the ₹66.48/KG we already pay Sayaji for identical Dextrose.
